A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the range of positron is not a simple function of the range of electrons, but depends on the material.
the range of positron is longer than that of electron for the same energy, and the ratio of the two ranges increases as the atomic number decreases.

The main takeaway from our work is that
positrons have a longer range than electrons of equal energy.
the range of 160 keV electrons in silver is only about 20 % larger than that of 40 keV electrons, while the range of 100 keV electrons in gold is only about 10 % larger than that in silver.
